narrative: OMX30 faces a mixed open following significant overnight deterioration in risk sentiment. The Nikkei's -5.66% collapse and Shanghai's -2.41% drop reflect broader Asia unwind, compounded by NASDAQ weakness (-1.33%) and a sharp 60bp rise in US 10Y yields to 4.724%. While the index remains 7.8% above its 200-MA in a technical bull market with strong ADX (25.2) and positive ROC-90 (+8.7%), the MACD rolling below signal and global correlation bias of -0.974% suggests momentum is stalling. Geopolitical tensions (Iran military escalation rhetoric, UAE trade suspension) are keeping VIX elevated at 15.19, which typically pressures equities. The jury is out on whether this is a healthy retracement or the start of a deeper pullback.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens into headwinds: Asia down hard, NASDAQ off 1.33%, yields ripping higher at 4.724%. Technicals show cracks—MACD below signal and Stochastic neutral (K=43.2)—though index remains well above 200-MA (+7.8%) and ADX is solidly bullish at 25.2. Watch 3123 (yesterday close) and 3085 (lower Bollinger band) as first support; resistance now 3180 (50-MA). Sectors diverge: Banks benefit from yield +60bp (wider NIM), but Tech/Telecom (Ericsson, Hexagon) suffer from NASDAQ selloff and DCF compression. Industrials pressured by oil +0.71% (input costs), but Volvo and Atlas Copco supported by USD/SEK strength (+0.15% to 9.521). Boliden and mining firms get modest lift from gold +0.58%, but watch copper (-0.43%) for mixed signals. Top risk: geopolitical escalation and potential VIX spike could trigger risk-off rotation into defensive plays (AstraZeneca, Essity). US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) key for sentiment reset.
